I will still farm from what I know works here, not from fancy talk. In Quzhou with well water, wheat and maize are my main food and cash base, so I will keep most of the land in the wheat-maize rotation and leave a smaller piece for cotton. I have done this many years, and I do not like cutting fertilizer too hard because if wheat turns yellow or maize stays short, the yield loss hurts more than spending a bit extra on inputs. Since I have 19.1 mu and some family labor is away working, I will keep the plan simple: stable wheat, stable summer maize, and a smaller cotton block I can still manage well. On wheat I will feed the crop enough nitrogen for tillering and grain filling, with phosphorus under the seed and some potassium because the land cannot just keep taking without putting back. On maize I will do a little heavier nitrogen because summer maize answers quickly after rain and water, and I will topdress in one shot when it is growing fast. Cotton is slower and more troublesome, so I will not plant too much of it, but I will still give it enough potassium and more pesticide sprays because insects are always the bigger problem there. I will use improved or hybrid seed where I have seen good field performance nearby, keep irrigation tied to key stages, and aim for steady yield instead of gambling.
